request.current_synthesis: Observation: M2 compiled the model with modest link masses, gear-5 motors without force limits, and measured high bounded-action accelerations; all tested impulse traces passively settle to near-zero velocity after release. Interpretation: insufficient actuator authority and persistent free-motion instability are not the leading initial explanations, although policy-induced overshoot remains possible. Observation: T1 trained a fresh PPO policy on the full 6–20 cm radius range, with training progress rising from zero to 0.58 success at checkpoint-120832. Limit: training progress is recipe-specific and does not establish development performance. Observation: M3 evaluated checkpoint-120832 at 93.75% on 160 held-out episodes. Of the ten failures, seven are at radii above 16 cm: five are non-reaches and two show repeated hold interruptions after first entry; three are inner-radius non-reaches. Interpretation: the initial concern that untrained inner radii dominate the gap is weakened for this candidate. The remaining gap is more consistent with outer-workspace approach conditioning, branch selection, singularity-adjacent trajectory generation, or policy-induced hold oscillation. M3 does not record final joint posture, branch residual, action, or velocity, so it cannot distinguish those mechanisms. No candidate role has been assigned and no official assessment has been requested.
request.decision_frontier: Which mechanism causes the residual outer-workspace failures—branch/singularity-adjacent reach generation, approach momentum and hold oscillation, or a broader policy-capacity/optimization limitation—and which PI-owned intervention can raise held-out success from 93.75% to at least 98% without sacrificing inner-radius performance? Discriminating evidence is outer-versus-inner evaluation with final branch residuals and, where possible, action/velocity or hold-interruption diagnostics. A candidate that reaches at least 98% on a fresh held-out panel with no concentrated outer-radius failure supports continuing toward official assessment; persistent outer non-reaches support branch-aware or outer-focused training/control changes; broad hold interruptions support stabilization-oriented reward or policy changes.
